nodes.name: FeP/Ni2P hybrid on Ni foam
aliases: FeP/Ni2P nanoparticles supported on Ni foam

nodes.name: First phosphidation (mainly Ni2P formation)
nodes.procedure: A commercially hydrophobic Ni foam was immersed into an aqueous Fe(NO3)3 solution (0.37 M), which was then converted to mainly Ni2P and a very small fraction of FeP at 450°C in Ar atmosphere, with phosphorus powder supplied upstream. After that, the samples were naturally cooled down under Ar gas protection, which became hydrophilic after first phosphidation.

unit_operations.name: Immersion
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: immersed a commercially hydrophobic Ni foam into an aqueous Fe(NO3)3 solution (0.37 M)

unit_operations.name: Phosphidation
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: converted to mainly Ni2P and a very small fraction of FeP at 450°C in Ar atmosphere, with phosphorus powder supplied upstream

unit_operations.name: Cooling
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: naturally cooled down under Ar gas protection

nodes.source_text: we first immersed a commercially hydrophobic Ni foam into an aqueous Fe(NO3)3 solution (0.37 M), which was then converted to mainly Ni2P and a very small fraction of FeP at 450°C in Ar atmosphere, with phosphorus powder supplied upstream. After that, the samples were naturally cooled down under Ar gas protection

nodes.name: Second phosphidation (FeP/Ni2P hybrid formation)
nodes.procedure: After first phosphidation, the samples were immersed into the Fe(NO3)3 solution (0.37 M) again. Then a second-time phosphidation was performed at 450°C in Ar atmosphere with phosphorus powder supplied upstream. The catalyst loading is around 8 mg cm^{-2} for the FeP/Ni2P catalyst.

unit_operations.name: Re-immersion
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: the samples were immersed into the Fe(NO3)3 solution again

nodes.source_text: In the following, a second-time phosphidation was performed after the samples were immersed into the Fe(NO3)3 solution again. The catalyst loading is around 8 mg cm^{-2} for the FeP/Ni2P catalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM reveals FeP and Ni₂P nanoparticles with diameters of 5-30 nm; interplanar spacings of 0.204 nm and 0.502 nm for Ni₂P (021) and (010) planes, and 0.181 nm and 0.193 nm for FeP (103) and (220) planes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: highresolution transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images (Fig. 1d, Supplementary Fig. 1), further reveal the nanoscale features of the FeP and Ni₂P particles with diameters of 5-30 nm. The interplanar spacings of these nanoparticles are resolved by TEM to be around 0.204 and 0.502 nm corresponding to the (021) and (010) planes of Ni₂P crystals, and 0.181 and 0.193 nm corresponding to the (103) and (220) planes of FeP crystals.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern confirms crystallinity of FeP/Ni₂P nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The selected area electron diffraction pattern (Fig. 1c), combined with highresolution transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM-EDX elemental mapping confirms homogeneous distribution of Ni, Fe, and P; EDX spectrum shows atomic ratio close to 2:1:2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: elemental mapping was carried out using TEM, confirming the homogenous distribution of Ni, Fe, and P elements in the FeP/Ni₂P nanoparticles (Fig. 1e). The energy dispersive X-ray (EDX) spectrum (Supplementary Fig. 2) shows that the Ni, Fe, and P elements are present with an atomic ratio close to 2:1:2

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS reveals P 2p metal phosphide doublets at 129.3/130.1 eV and phosphate at 133.5/134.3 eV; Fe 2p3/2 peaks at 707.0 eV (FeP), 709.9 eV (oxide), 711.9 eV (phosphate); Ni 2p3/2 at 853.6 eV (Ni2P), 856.4 eV (Ni-POx); surface oxidation ~74.8% for FeP, ~13.5% for Ni2P nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The P 2p core level spectrum can be fit with two doublets (Fig. 1f), with one located at the binding energies of 129.3 and 130.1 eV attributing to phosphorus anions of metal phosphides, and the other at 133.5 and 134.3 eV indicative of phosphate-like P... The XPS spectrum of Fe 2p3/2 core level (Supplementary Fig. 3a) can be deconvoluted into three main peaks with binding energies of 707.0, 709.9, and 711.9 eV... This peak deconvolution is also applied to the Ni 2p3/2 core level spectrum (Supplementary Fig. 3b), where three binding energies located at 853.6, 856.4, and 861.0 eV... According to the survey spectrum (Supplementary Fig. 4) and distribution quantification (Supplementary Table 1), it is estimated that the percentage of surface oxidized species in FeP nanoparticles is close to 74.8%, and the percentage in Ni2P is around 13.5%

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms FeP (ICSD-633046) and Ni₂P (ICSD-646102) phases with characteristic peaks; strongest Ni foam peaks at 45° and 52°.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A typical XRD pattern (Fig. 1g) reveals the main indexes from the as-prepared FeP/Ni₂P hybrid and Ni foam support. The two strongest peaks at 45° and 52° are mainly originated from the Ni foam support (ICSD-53809). All the other peaks are the characteristic ones of FeP (ICSD-633046) and Ni₂P (ICSD-646102)

nodes.characterization_summary: Cdl = 19.3 mF cm⁻² for FeP/Ni₂P hybrid (OER); Cdl = 907.8 mF cm⁻² (HER), indicating high electrochemically active surface area.
